title: Regression triage: flash+paged-KV+cont-batch eval summary
body:
Purpose:
Quick triage of regression observed after landing runtime change that enables paged-KV + continuous-batching in the flash-attention codepath. This doc captures the A/B evals we ran, the diffs, short examples of failure modes, hypotheses, and next steps for rollout/fix. Goal is actionable triage for SRE/runtime + applied-ML to decide: revert, patch, or mitigate with fallback rules.

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- Perf: Cont-batching + paged-KV reduced P95 token latency by ~12–18% on long-context workloads and increased end-to-end throughput by ~25% on aggregate.
- Cost: Per-token GPU time went down ~15% for 8k+ contexts due to fewer redundant KV passes.
- Quality regressions: We observed a measurable drop in some multi-turn QA and long-form summarization metrics: QA-F1 drop ~2.4 points (relative), factuality/hallucination rate up by ~3.1 percentage points on the long-horizon prompt set.
- Failure modes: Regressions concentrated in (a) multi-turn stateful conversations where small context-preserving differences accumulate, (b) long-instruction summarization (>= 4k tokens) where the paged-KV retrieval policy appears to evict prefixes that model expects to reference, and (c) constrained decoding cases (exact-match prompts) where cont-batching merged micro-batches and caused subtle timing/seed differences that affect top-k decoding.
- Recommendation: Disable cont-batching for routes marked "strict-consistency" and add a diagnostic flag to record per-request KV-page hit/miss. Continue experiments on a small canary with paged-KV only and cont-batch disabled to isolate cause.

Setup and test harness:
- Branch: runtime/pagedkv-contbatch-opt (merge landed 2026-03-08).
- Models: open/model-x-large-v1 (causal decoder); verified similar delta on model-y-13b-quant.
- Hardware: A100-80GB and H100 pool; observed similar qualitative diffs across both but numbers slightly better on H100.
- Eval harness: redwood-evals v0.9.3 (configs: --promptset long-horizon-qna, --seed 42, --stream false, --sampling top_p=0.9,temp=0.0 for exact-match runs).
- Prompt sets used (short):
  - long-horizon-qna: 1.2k examples, 30–12k token contexts, multi-turn QA, mostly Wiki-derived and customer-simulated chat sessions.
  - convo-state-check: 850 examples, 3–8 turns each, tests persistence of entity references and pronoun resolution across turns.
  - summarization-long: 400 examples, 4k–10k token inputs, golden abstractive summaries.

Key metrics (aggregated diffs, baseline = 'flash-only' runtime with cont-batch off, current = 'flash+pagedkv+contbatch'):
- long-horizon-qna:
  - QA-F1: baseline 79.6 -> current 77.2 (delta -2.4)
  - Exact-match (short answer): baseline 61.4 -> current 59.8 (delta -1.6)
  - Hallucination rate (annotated): baseline 8.5% -> current 11.6% (delta +3.1%)
- convo-state-check:
  - Reference-resolve accuracy: baseline 88.1 -> current 85.3 (delta -2.8)
  - Entity-drop incidents (automated metric): baseline 2.3% -> current 5.7% (delta +3.4%)
- summarization-long:
  - ROUGE-L: baseline 41.7 -> current 40.1 (delta -1.6)
  - Human brevity/factuality score (sampled 60 examples): baseline 4.1/5.0 -> current 3.7/5.0 (delta -0.4)

Latency / throughput (representative):
- 8k context end-to-end p95 generation latency: baseline 1240ms -> current 1038ms (improvement -16.3%)
- tokens/sec aggregate (mixed workloads): baseline 210 TPS -> current 265 TPS (+26%)
- GPU utilization (A100 jobs): baseline 68% -> current 79% (more efficient kernel packing)

Detailed observations and examples:
1) Context eviction pattern (paged-KV behavior):
- Symptom: In several summarization-long tests the model started referencing only last 2–3k tokens, misattributing earlier facts (hallucinations).
- Repro snippet (from prompt id LH-322):
  - Prompt: long article with timeline of events (9k tokens). Golden summary: mentions events A->B->C.
  - Baseline output: correctly lists events A, B, C in order with dates.
  - Current output: omits event B, invents event D between A and C (hallucinated).
- Hypothesis: paged-KV's eviction policy uses a size heuristic that, combined with cont-batch conflation, delays refilling the in-GPU KV cache for pages containing earlier context, so the attention weights shift to more recent pages.

2) Multi-turn pronoun drop in conversation:
- Symptom: For 3–6 turn queries where user refers back to an entity introduced in turn 1, model substituted a generic descriptor or dropped the reference entirely in 4.5% of cases under current runtime vs 1.4% baseline.
- Example (conv id CS-78):
  - Turn1: "I booked a flight to Lisbon on June 5th with Delta."
  - Turn4 (user): "What was the carrier again?"
  - Baseline: "Delta."
  - Current: "The airline." (loss of core entity)
- Hypothesis: cont-batch sharding merges KV updates from micro-batches; ordering/latency differences cause the decoder to see slightly different cached keys at decode time.

3) Constrained decoding mismatch (deterministic settings):
- Symptom: Exact-match prompts (policy templates) that previously produced canonical tokens now show off-by-one token differences in ~1% of runs. These differences cascade into failures in downstream validators.
- Root cause theory: cont-batch merges and reorders micro-batches for better GPU occupancy; tiny timing differences plus uint8 quantization rounding can push the top-k boundary when temp==0.0.

Repro steps to isolate cause:
- Run eval harness with contbatch disabled on the new runtime binary (env override: REDWOOD_RUNTIME_CONT_BATCH=0) while keeping paged-KV enabled. Observe whether QA-F1 and hallucination regressions persist.
- Run paged-KV disabled but contbatch enabled (env: REDWOOD_RUNTIME_PAGED_KV=0).
- Run both disabled (should match baseline).
- Capture per-request KV stats (number of page loads, evictions, page-hit ratio) and export paired outputs for diffing.
- Use seed sweep (42, 87, 101) to confirm not seed-sensitive.

Immediate triage actions taken so far (what we've tried):
- Rolled a canary of 5% traffic with current runtime to observe real-traffic incidence (observed 3.2x higher support tickets for hallucination in canary routes in first 24h).
- Added per-request diagnostic logging to record KV page hits/misses and batch composition.
- Created a targeted test set for contested cases (200 examples) and ran pairwise diffs to produce minimal repro cases.

Open hypotheses prioritized: 
- H1 (paged-KV eviction tuning): eviction threshold too aggressive for long-horizon docs and is discarding important prefix pages. Likelihood: high.
- H2 (cont-batch merging semantics): micro-batch reordering/merging introduces nondeterminism for deterministic decodes; interplay with quantization edges causes rare top-k shifts. Likelihood: medium-high.
- H3 (kernel numerical differences): new kernel selection produces different FP/INT accumulation order causing tiny logits changes that cascade. Likelihood: medium.

Proposed immediate mitigations: 
- Config flag per-route to opt-out of cont-batching (fast to ship via routing config in the console). Mark existing QA-heavy customer routes as "strict-consistency" by default for next 48h.
- Tune paged-KV eviction policy: increase retention window for prefetched pages when context length > 4k. Start with +1x retention for pages beyond 4k and measure.
- Add deterministic micro-batch boundary enforcement for temp==0.0/beam decoding modes.

Longer-term work items: 
- Rigorous numeric sensitivity tests across quantization configurations and kernel choices (owned by applied-ml + runtime).
- Build a synthetic meta-eval that incrementally increases context length and measures per-page importance via gradient-based saliency to guide eviction heuristics.
- Improve rollout tooling: automatic rollback triggers if hallucination rate crosses +2% vs baseline on canary.

Action items (owners):
- Marco Chen: run cont-batch-off vs paged-kv-on canary (due 2026-03-14).
- Aisha Patel: create tuned eviction config and run the long-horizon suite, produce numbers (due 2026-03-16).
- Dana Rivera: add per-route flag and patch console to expose "cont-batch: off" for customers (PR + tests) (due 2026-03-15).
- Luis Martínez: numeric sensitivity sweep across quant levels (8-bit/4-bit) (due 2026-03-18).

Notes / questions for runtime owners: 
- Can we export finer-grained timeline traces (kernel start/end, page load times) for a single request from the canary? This will help line up eviction with observed hallucinations.
- Is there a cheap fallback (at runtime) that can detect high page-eviction activity and switch to a "no-cont-batch" mode for that request shape?

Attachments / artifact locations: 
- Minimal repro set and paired outputs: gs://redwood-evals/pagedkv-contbatch-repro/2026-03-11/
- Full eval run logs (jsonl): gs://redwood-evals/pagedkv-contbatch-fullrun/2026-03-11/
- Canary dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/canary/flash-pkv-contbatch-2026-03

Conclusion:
The runtime change delivers meaningful performance gains but exposes a real risk to quality for long-horizon and multi-turn conversational workloads. We should avoid wholesale rollout until we can either (a) patch eviction/ordering issues that explain the quality regressions, or (b) implement conservative route-based defaults that keep cont-batch off for customers who need deterministic outputs. Next milestone: determine if paged-KV-only (no cont-batching) reproduces regressions; if not, cont-batch merging semantics are primary suspect and should be reverted for strict routes.

Appendix: raw sample diffs (one example each)
- LH-322 baseline:
  "On June 3rd, the committee approved motion A, followed by Motion B on June 12th, and Motion C on July 1st."
- LH-322 current:
  "On June 3rd, the committee approved motion A, then later Motion D was added and Motion C occurred in July."

- CS-78 baseline turn4: "Delta."
- CS-78 current turn4: "The airline."

(End of doc)
